text: A comparator this literature has not used
scope: the learned-routing-for-LEO line surveyed in Section II
evidence: occupied-check 17/08/2026 over arXiv (learned routing / GNN / DRL / MARL for LEO, 2024-2026) and the nearest work arXiv:2601.21921; none reports a tolerance-based blind multipath baseline at a matched budget
not_claimed: that no paper anywhere uses eps-ECMP as a baseline; ECMP is standard in terrestrial TE. The claim is about this specific line of work
how_it_could_be_wrong: a paper outside the searched keywords, or one that reports such a baseline without naming it

text: Second, and previously unremarked, the decoder's softmin temperature is not a constant of the method
scope: papers that amortize a traffic equilibrium with a learned price field and decode by softmin splitting
evidence: the nearest work does not report a temperature sweep; our own prior version fixed it at 0.2 without stating so
not_claimed: that temperature sensitivity is unknown in soft-assignment literature generally, where it is well studied
how_it_could_be_wrong: any paper in this line that swept it and we did not find

text: with inter-satellite delays taking continuous values, exact cost ties essentially never occur, and to our knowledge this is unremarked
scope: the +Grid inter-satellite topologies used in this paper and in the LEO routing literature we surveyed
evidence: measured: 0 of 2620 node-destination pairs had two out-edges of exactly equal cost on the 132-satellite shell
not_claimed: that no LEO topology can have ties; a topology with quantised or uniform link lengths would have many
how_it_could_be_wrong: operators quantise ISL delays in practice, which would create ties and make textbook ECMP meaningful again. We say so in Section VII
